That's not really the FBI claiming to be above the law. This is the judicial process at work. During the discovery phase the prosecution is required to present all of the evidence they intend to use against the accused. If they fail to do so to the satisfaction of the courts then the case runs the risk of being dismissed due to insufficient evidence to warrant a trial. The FBI is stating that they'd rather allow the case to be dismissed than make certain information public knowledge. In this case the FBI has decided that it's better to let one accused man go free instead of providing potentially hostile actors with information they're using in active investigations. The bottom line is that the government can get away with a lot of fucked up shit to gather evidence, but due to the fact that we have certain constitutional protections they can't use it to secure criminal convictions unless they're willing to bring everything to the table.
